question: Two trains having lengths of 160 m and 140 m are running at speeds of 100 km/hr and 130 km/hr, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
solution:
**Given:**

Length of first train = 160 m

Length of second train = 140 m

Speed of first train = 100 km/hr

Speed of second train = 130 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed (same direction) = Speed of faster train − Speed of slower train

Time taken = Total distance ÷ Relative speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Relative speed = 130 − 100 = 30 km/hr

⇒ Convert relative speed to m/s: 30 × (1000 ÷ 3600) = 25/3 m/s

⇒ Total distance = Length of first train + Length of second train = 160 + 140 = 300 m

⇒ Time taken = Total distance ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Time taken = 300 ÷ (25/3)

⇒ Time taken = 300 × (3 ÷ 25)

⇒ Time taken = 900 ÷ 25

⇒ Time taken = 36 seconds

⇒ Convert time to minutes: 36 ÷ 60 = 0.6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 0.6 minutes.**
